one_liner: Pure-Go Schonhage-Strassen multiplication for math/big integers: 3-25x faster than math/big from 1 Mbit, 1.2-3x slower than GMP.
what_it_does: Adds FFT-based multiplication and a subquadratic decimal parser to Go's math/big. The API is two functions on *big.Int: bigfft.Mul(x, y) returns a new product and falls back to big.Int.Mul unless both operands exceed 1800 words, and bigfft.FromDecimalString(s) parses a non-negative base-10 string. It is not a drop-in for the math/big methods: callers must route their large multiplications through bigfft.Mul explicitly.
how_it_is_fast: Schonhage-Strassen: operands are cut into 2^k chunks and transformed with a recursive radix-2 FFT over the ring Z/(2^n+1) (fermat.go), where roots of unity are powers of two, so twiddle multiplications are bit shifts (with a sqrt(2) half-shift trick). Pointwise products are a single level that calls math/big's Karatsuba, not a recursive FFT. Inner loops reuse math/big's assembly kernels (addVV, subVV, mulAddVWW and others) via go:linkname. FromDecimalString splits the string in halves and multiplies by precomputed powers of 10, so parsing cost follows multiplication cost instead of math/big's quadratic digit loop.
when_to_use: A pure-Go program (no cgo) that multiplies integers of roughly 1 Mbit or more: README shows 3.7x at 1 Mbit and 24.9x at 100 Mbit over math/big on a Core 2 Quad (derived from page data).

Parsing decimal strings of 100,000+ digits into big.Int: 12x faster at 1e6 digits and 56x at 1e7 digits than SetString on a Core i5-4590 (derived from benchmarks/scan.*), with about 53x less allocation at 1e6 digits.
Number-theory or pi-digit experiments in Go where cgo bindings to GMP are not allowed.
Already pulled in transitively (modernc.org/sqlite uses it, per issue #22) and you want FFT products for your own big multiplications too.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ code: GMP is faster at every size the README measured (1.2x to 3.1x; bigfft 1.85x slower at 1 Mbit and 1.96x slower at 100 Mbit, derived from page data), and FLINT is faster still.
Operands below about 1 Mbit: math/big is equal or faster; in the Go 1.8 run, bigfft.Mul at 1 kbit took 525 ns vs math/big's 298 ns (1.76x slower, derived from benchmarks/bench and bench.big).
Division, modular exponentiation, GCD or decimal output: only multiplication and decimal input are provided (division request issue #20 is open).
Production code that needs a maintained dependency: the author's README calls it a toy proof of concept, the last commit is 2023-01-29, and 5 issues and 4 PRs (loong64, gccgo, wasm) sit unanswered.

gccgo builds: the package reaches into math/big's internal kernels with go:linkname, and the 2021 gccgo build fix (PR #14) was never merged; gccgo support after the 2023 linkname switch is not documented.

integration.dependencies: none outside the Go standard library (math/big internals via go:linkname)
integration.min_toolchain: go.mod says go 1.12; CI was set up for Go 1.12, 1.17 and latest in January 2023
integration.platforms: any GOARCH of the standard gc toolchain since the January 2023 switch from per-arch assembly stubs to go:linkname (no .s files remain in the repo root); gccgo not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Mul and FromDecimalString keep no package-level mutable state in fft.go/scan.go (each call allocates its own buffers), so concurrent calls on distinct inputs look safe, but this is not stated
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — bigfft.Mul(x, y) has the same semantics as new(big.Int).Mul(x, y) but every call site must be changed, and it always allocates a fresh result

gotchas: Depends on go:linkname into math/big internals (addVV, subVV, addVW, subVW, shlVU, mulAddVWW, addMulVVW). Go master keeps these symbols explicitly for bigfft ('hall of shame' comments citing go.dev/issue/67401), so builds work today, but the package relies on Go not removing them.
FromDecimalString ignores the ok result of big.Int.SetString on each chunk and expects digits only: no sign, no error return, so malformed input yields a wrong number rather than an error.
The FFT path switches on at 1800 words (about 115 kbit on 64-bit), a hard-coded package variable; the README says 200 kbits. Below that, Mul just calls math/big and adds an allocation.
Old releases (pseudo-version v0.0.0-20170806...) used assembly jump stubs and fail on some setups with 'missing function body' (issue #21); use the 2023 commit.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick bigfft only in pure Go with Mbit-scale operands; holiman/uint256 is the Go sibling for fixed 256-bit math, and for C/C++ FLINT or GMP itself beat bigfft at every size, as do the GPU/NTT multipliers (TzdLanguage) on huge operands.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Go benchmarks: on a Core 2 Quad Q8200 (Go version unstated), multiplication of equal-size random integers is 3.7x faster than math/big at 1 Mbit and 24.9x at 100 Mbit, but 1.85x-1.96x slower than GMP; a later Go 1.8 run on a Core i5-4590 (benchmarks/ directory) shows 3.0x-28.8x over math/big and 2.0x-2.6x slower than GMP 6.1.2 (gmpbench), all derived from page data. Decimal scanning is 12x faster than SetString at 1e6 digits on the i5-4590.
status_note: Abandoned since January 2023 and self-described as a toy, but BSD-3-Clause, about 700 lines of Go (4 source files), used in production by modernc.org/sqlite (issue #22) and kept building because Go's math/big preserves its linkname targets.
